blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.stem_clinical_pattern: CDC Diagnosis and MedlinePlus Description directly support feeding-related respiratory symptoms and failure of a tube to pass to the stomach.
claim_audit.gastric_air: NCBI Pathophysiology directly supports air entering the stomach when esophageal atresia is associated with tracheoesophageal fistula.
claim_audit.correct_mechanism: MedlinePlus Description directly supports failed normal separation of the embryonic esophagus and trachea.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NCBI Pathophysiology: failed duodenal recanalization causes duodenal atresia.
claim_audit.distractor_2: NCBI Development/Pathophysiology: abnormal neural-crest-derived enteric ganglion development underlies Hirschsprung disease.
claim_audit.distractor_3: NCBI Pathophysiology: failure of abdominal contents to return produces omphalocele.
claim_audit.distractor_4: NCBI Development/Pathophysiology: persistent vitelline duct produces vitelline-duct remnants/fistula.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The stem independently localizes an obstruction to the proximal esophagus and the gastric air requires an airway-to-distal-esophagus route; among the five mechanisms, only abnormal tracheoesophageal separation explains both findings.
adversarial_second_pass.h_type_tef_challenge: H-type TEF alone would not make an orogastric tube terminate in the upper esophagus, so it is not an alternative explanation.
adversarial_second_pass.isolated_esophageal_atresia_challenge: Isolated esophageal atresia explains failed tube passage but not gastric air; the distal fistula configuration explains both.
adversarial_second_pass.distractor_challenge: Each distractor maps to a different congenital GI developmental defect and none explains proximal esophageal discontinuity plus gastric air.
